:::{#thm-prediction-error}
#### Expected squared prediction error

Let $Y_0 = f(x_0) + \noise$,
where $f$ is a fixed function,
$\noise$ has $\E{\noise} = 0$ and $\Var{\noise} = \varpar$,
and $\noise$ is independent of the prediction $\hat f(x_0)$,
which has $\E{\hat f(x_0)^2} < \infty$.
Then

$$\E{\paren{Y_0 - \hat f(x_0)}^2} = \sqf{\bias{\hat f(x_0)}} + \Var{\hat f(x_0)} + \varpar$$

:::

::: proof

Write $Y_0 - \hat f(x_0) = \noise + D$,
where $D \eqdef f(x_0) - \hat f(x_0)$.
Expanding the square and using linearity of expectation,

$$
\ba
\E{\paren{Y_0 - \hat f(x_0)}^2}
&= \E{\noise^2} + 2\E{\noise D} + \E{D^2}
&& \text{(expand the square)}
\ea
$$

- $\E{\noise^2} = \varpar$,
  by @sol-noise-second-moment.
- $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \E{\noise D} &= \E{\noise}\E{D} \\
  &= 0,
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  because $\noise$ is independent of $\hat f(x_0)$,
  hence of $D$,
  and $\E{\noise} = 0$.
- By @thm-variance,
  $\E{D^2} = \Var{D} + \sqf{\E{D}}$.
  Here $\Var{D} = \Var{\hat f(x_0)}$,
  because $f(x_0)$ is a constant,
  and

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \E{D} &= f(x_0) - \E{\hat f(x_0)} \\
  &= -\bias{\hat f(x_0)},
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  so $\sqf{\E{D}} = \sqf{\bias{\hat f(x_0)}}$.

Adding the three terms gives the claim.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-irreducible-error}
#### Irreducible error

In @thm-prediction-error,
the term $\varpar = \Var{\noise}$ is the **irreducible error**.
It does not depend on the prediction $\hat f$,
so no choice of prediction can remove it.
For example, in @exr-prediction-error, $\varpar = 3$,
so every prediction there has expected squared error at least $3$.

:::

::: {.remark .notes}

This expected prediction error decomposition into squared bias, variance, and irreducible error follows @james2021islr2e [Section 2.2.2].

:::
